title: Construct explicit bounded dyadic norm-six feature evaluation
body:
PR5084 proves that the norm-six kernel has at most19,600 dyadic factor pairs, but its full-shell matrix factorization does not give source-independent feature formulas or coefficient/evaluation bounds. This package constructs those formulas directly from PR2222's actual P48p Gram and19648 integer-valued cubic features. It does not improve the already established term count.

The48 shell relations admit an explicit dyadic pivot minor:21 mixed-cubic pivots of coefficient4 and27 linear pivots of coefficient1 or2, followed by one anchor substitution. The resulting54996 nonzero transform coefficients are quarter-integral, with scaled magnitude at most48 and target accumulation mass52. The19600 retained source features are integer-valued; target features are integer numerators over256. A written polynomial argument proves the kernel identity for every integral norm-six source and every integral target. No shell enumeration or full-shell elimination is used.

The proof includes descriptor generation, coefficient height, evaluation prefixes, integer operations and indexed workspace bounds. A target uses at most96596 integer multiplications,116244 additions/subtractions and48 exact divisions by3, with19712 integer workspace slots and a fixed descriptor of at most245884 integer slots. These are arithmetic-model upper bounds, not a tape-placement or Python-heap claim. The inherited norm-six geometry and binary chart remain explicit dependencies. Physical source acquisition, I-K side program, frames, arbitrary-dirty restoration, routing, matched bit supplier and compiler/outer admission remain unknown; the algebraic support bound960400 is unchanged, and no kappa or selected-frontier update is claimed.

Validation: registered CPython3.12.2 replay passes all48 independent polynomial ideal identities, coefficient bounds,988 complete pairings using the26 original actual-Gram shell vectors plus12 wider targets, and six semantic controls. Separate AI review independently checks the pivot determinant and formal assignments. Committed-byte/source-history and official15-payload-file export checks pass. Git-free optimized replay passes in2.21seconds with all16 exported files unchanged; actual source drift and a bool/int result-type mutation both reject, with every byte restored. No heavy, full-shell, native, Lean or selected historical replay was run.

Credit Cinna Davis PR2222 for the kernel, features and Gram; DreamingOfClouds PR2244 for the rational rank perspective; Dugongue PR4494 for dyadic factorization; Nick Petalas PR5084 for the existence theorem and constructive open question; Nebe/Sloane and the retained Leech/Niemeier lineage. New work by JoyboyBrian with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, Apache-2.0. Separate AI review is not independent human or proof-kernel acceptance.
